messages.text: Price makes undisputed history as she shuts out Kotaskova

metadata.summary: Lauren Price made history for Welsh boxing when she beat Michaela Kotaskova to become the undisputed welterweight world champion.
metadata.content: Lauren Price makes boxing history for Wales with first undisputed championship win as she shuts out Michaela Kotaskova | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lauren Price makes boxing history for Wales with first undisputed championship win as she shuts out Michaela Kotaskova Lauren Price beat Michaela Kotaskova at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff to become the undisputed welterweight world champion; winning a unanimous decision saw Price add the WBO title to the WBA, WBC and IBF belts she already had; Price is Wales' first undisputed champion in the four-belt era Friday 20 November 2026 23:28, UK Image: Lauren Price became the undisputed welterweight world champion (Photos: Chris Dean/Boxxer) Lauren Price made history for Welsh boxing when she beat Michaela Kotaskova to become the undisputed welterweight world champion. With a unanimous decision victory over Kotaskova at the Utilita Arena, a shutout 100-90 for all three judges, Price added the vacant WBO 147lbs title to the IBF, WBC and WBA belts. An Olympic gold medallist in 2021, Price is the first Welsh boxer to become an undisputed world champion in the four-belt era. The first female British champion too, the skilful southpaw started busily and with intent. She planted stiff left crosses through the middle, that back hand arrowing between Kotaskova's gloves and catching her chin. Price stamped her authority on the fight, teeing off with flurries. metadata.summary: Formula 1 will return to V8 engines from 2030 in a move FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has described as "an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA" of the sport.
metadata.content: V8 engines returning to Formula 1 in 2030 as FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem describes move to 'reconnect with DNA' of the sport | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content V8 engines returning to Formula 1 in 2030 as FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem describes move to 'reconnect with DNA' of the sport Multiple Formula 1 drivers had backed for V8 engines to return to the sport; FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has confirmed V8 engines will return from 2030 after a 17-year absence; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Friday 20 November 2026 20:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Formula 1 will return to V8 engines from 2030 in a move FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has described as "an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA" of the sport. Earlier this week, Ben Sulayem teased the possibility of V8 engines ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1 , with the sound of a screaming F1 car with a caption: "You spoke, we listened. V8s coming soon." On Friday, the FIA announced a technical framework had been unanimously agreed between the FIA, Formula One Management (FOM), the teams and Formula 1 power unit manufacturers to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 power unit.
